pointers.sentence: `convert_exception_to_response` takes a callable and returns a function that calls it inside a `try` and, if it raises an `Exception`, returns what `response_for_exception` makes of the request and the exception (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:convert_exception_to_response`).
`BaseHandler.load_middleware` applies it to the centre and to every middleware as it builds the chain (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.load_middleware`).

The docstring of `convert_exception_to_response` says it is applied to all middleware so that "the next middleware in the stack can rely on getting a response instead of an exception", and DEP 5, which brought in `settings.MIDDLEWARE`, that a middleware "should always get back a response" (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:convert_exception_to_response`, `deps:final/0005-improved-middleware.rst`).

The docstring of `convert_exception_to_response` says it is applied to all middleware so that "the next middleware in the stack can rely on getting a response instead of an exception", and DEP 5, which brought in `settings.MIDDLEWARE`, that a middleware "should always get back a response" (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:convert_exception_to_response`, `deps:final/0005-improved-middleware.rst`).

The centre calls them ([The centre of the chain](view.md)): each is offered the exception, innermost middleware first, and the first to return a response ends the matter (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.process_exception_by_middleware`).

DEP 5's stricter layering confined them to what the view raises, or a `TemplateResponse`'s `render`, and made a middleware's exception a response at once (`deps:final/0005-improved-middleware.rst`, `docs/releases/1.10.txt`).

DEP 5's stricter layering confined them to what the view raises, or a `TemplateResponse`'s `render`, and made a middleware's exception a response at once (`deps:final/0005-improved-middleware.rst`, `docs/releases/1.10.txt`).
An **error view** in the table is one of four views that a project can replace; the next heading describes them (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:response_for_exception`).

For these `response_for_exception` first calls `HttpRequest._mark_post_parse_error`, which gives the request an empty `POST` and an empty `FILES`, so that the error view or the debug page can read them without parsing the data again and raising the same exception (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest._mark_post_parse_error`).

`response_for_exception` logs the response through `log_response`, with the exception attached, for every class but `Http404`, and a response is logged once ([Logging](../startup/logging.md#log_response-a-response-is-logged-once)) (`django/utils/log.py:log_response`).

An error view is found by `URLResolver.resolve_error_handler`, in the current URLconf or among Django's defaults ([The error views](../views/errors.md#found-through-the-urlconf-called-like-a-view)) (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver.resolve_error_handler`).

If the error view itself raises, the failure is treated as an unrecognised exception, the signal sent and `handle_uncaught_exception` taking over: a broken 404 page becomes a 500 (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:get_exception_response`).

If `settings.DEBUG_PROPAGATE_EXCEPTIONS` is true it raises the exception again; otherwise, if `settings.DEBUG` is true, it returns `technical_500_response`, the debug page with the traceback ([The debug pages and `ExceptionReporter`](../views/debug.md)); otherwise it calls the 500 error view, with the request alone (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:handle_uncaught_exception`).

An exception raised before the chain is entered can reach the server too, since the wrappers, part of the chain, cannot catch what happens outside it: a malformed `Content-Type` header, for one, raises `BadRequest` while the request object is being made (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest._set_content_type_params`).
